prerequisites: Fundamentals of differential and integral calculus, including partial differential equations and theorems related to surface and volume integrals (Green, Gauss, Stokes, etc.)
Thorough knowledge of physics fundamentals with particular reference to mechanics and its principles

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamental principles and ability to understand fluid dynamic phenomena.
Ability to apply acquired knowledge in the design and practice of modeling and analysis of processes involving hydrostatics and fluid motion.
Ability to find and use data to formulate responses to well-defined concrete or abstract problems.
Ability to communicate about the phenomena described above with the recipients of the studies and simulations, and with those who develop and use simulation models.
Ability to undertake more advanced studies with some autonomy on particular phenomenological aspects.

syllabus_topics: Principles and equations of compressible fluid mechanics
assessment_rules: The written exam verifies the ability to apply learned notions to engineering problems. The oral exam assesses learning objectives, particularly theoretical knowledge acquired and its application, with special reference to the ability to tackle new problems. The grade, expressed in thirtieths, is assigned proportionally to the overall achievement of these objectives.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Meccanica E Gestionale (First Level Degree In Mechanical And Management Engineering), classe L-9 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria industriale
